classification.difficultyReason: Calculate the lower three-standard-deviation boundary and interpret it against a manufacturer's minimum-weight guarantee.

content.prompt:
A canned fruit manufacturer guarantees minimum weight 250 g.
The cans have mean 252.5 g and standard deviation 0.4 g. Is the guarantee realistic? Why?

answer.short: Yes, realistically: $\mu-3\sigma=251.3\text{ g}>250\text{ g}$, so almost all cans should exceed 250 g.
answer.worked:
Using the empirical rule, approximately 99.7% of weights lie within three standard deviations of the mean.
$$\begin{aligned}\mu-3\sigma&=252.5-3(0.4)\\&=251.3\text{ g}\\\mu+3\sigma&=252.5+3(0.4)\\&=253.7\text{ g}\end{aligned}$$
Since the lower boundary, 251.3 g, exceeds 250 g, almost all cans should exceed the guaranteed weight. The guarantee is realistic in practice, although this does not establish an absolute minimum.

spec.mathematics: Mean 252.5 g; standard deviation 0.4 g; central empirical-rule interval 251.3 to 253.7 g.
